idiom_name: accumulator argument that every collaborating method appends to
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: create the accumulator in the caller - the only place that knows the final shape - and pass the same object to each collaborating method, which appends its part through a minimal add/append protocol; the caller consumes the result once the call tree returns. Type the parameter as narrowly as the appenders need (an append method rather than the concrete collection) and name it for direction ('out', 'into', 'sink'). Prefer returning a value when only one producer contributes, and keep the accumulator confined to one invocation so it never outlives the collaboration that fills it.
code_sketch:
result = new Accumulator()
render(node, result)       # several callees append their part
collect(node, result)
report = result.finish()   # the caller alone consumes the result
pitfalls: Appenders reading, clearing or re-ordering the accumulator break the single-owner contract that made the pattern safe.
A shared accumulator reused across invocations accumulates stale results; give every traversal its own instance.
No thread-safety: concurrent producers need per-producer accumulators plus a merge, or a concurrent collector type.
